correctness.rationale: The source-specific step is reconstructed from the mapping-torus model: each Weierstrass orbit of length \(r_j\) traces one connected curve of projection degree \(r_j\), hence its branch torus has class \(r_jA\). Excision and the Thom isomorphism reduce the complement calculation to the intersection map \(H_2(T^2\times S^2;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z^c\), whose image is generated by the orbit-length vector. The resulting extension splits over the free group \(\mathbb Z^2\), and one-row Smith normal form gives the stated free rank and gcd torsion. The bundled checker verifies finite arithmetic consequences but is not used as the universal proof.

value.rationale: The branch complement is a natural object in the construction, and its first homology is the first abelian invariant controlling meridians and covering characters. The formula translates monodromy orbit arithmetic into exact topological torsion: transitive orbit gives maximal cyclic torsion, a fixed Weierstrass point kills all meridional torsion, and intermediate partitions are measured by their gcd. This is a structural all-family statement rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
